findings.text: Native directory record carries four logical parts with the inode holder linked to d_ino and the position holder linked to d_off and the length holder linked to d_reclen and the name area linked to d_name. Length governs spacing to the next record and the final byte of each record carries the entry type tag.

Emission state for the native call joins an iteration context known as ctx with a user buffer cursor known as current_dir plus a remembered prior length known as prev_reclen plus a sticky failure slot known as error. The cursor advances as records are emitted and the prior length supports later fixup of the preceding position.

Emission state for the wide call mirrors the native state with an iteration context plus a cursor aimed at wide records plus a remembered prior length plus a sticky failure slot. It preserves the same accounting relationship between cursor advance and remaining capacity.

Old compatibility record holds an inode value linked to d_ino plus a position value linked to d_offset plus an explicit name length linked to d_namlen plus a trailing name area linked to d_name. It describes a single entry rather than a packed stream.

Old compatibility emission state joins an iteration context with a single user record pointer plus a numeric outcome holder. The outcome doubles as a completion flag that prevents a second emission in the same call.

Compatibility packed record carries an inode value plus a position value plus a record length plus a trailing name area, with the type tag kept in the last byte of the record. Widths follow the compatibility word size rather than the native word size.

Compatibility packed emission state combines an iteration context with a user cursor plus a remembered prior length plus a sticky failure slot, preserving the same cursor and fixup discipline as the native path.

Poll wait storage forms a chain where each page links to an older page through next and tracks allocation through an entry cursor over a trailing flexible area. Fullness is judged by whether the next allocation address would pass the page bound, prompting allocation of a further page.

Select bitset bundle groups six word arrays with requested readability plus requested writability plus requested exception standing alongside three parallel result arrays for the same three classes. Access helpers select per word slices for input and output and exception and merge request words to detect interest.

Native directory listing entry accepts a descriptor plus a user buffer plus a byte capacity, iterates the open directory through its emitter, then finalizes the last record position and reports bytes placed. An empty file reference yields a bad descriptor failure and user write problems yield a fault failure.

Wide directory listing entry provides the same contract as the native entry but targets wide records with full width inode and type members. It finalizes the trailing position from the iteration position and reports bytes placed or a negative failure.

Old compatibility listing entry handles one record per call using a single record pointer and a unit capacity hint to the filesystem. It returns the emitter outcome when set and otherwise propagates the iteration outcome, with bad descriptor on empty file reference.

Compatibility packed listing entry accepts a descriptor plus a compatibility buffer plus a capacity, iterates through its compatibility emitter, then finalizes the last record position and reports bytes placed. Failure modes mirror the native entry.

Range remap preparation entry forwards input and output file positions plus a length pointer plus flags to a shared internal helper with an empty extra context, returning that helper outcome unchanged.

Packed emitters maintain cursor accounting where success consumes aligned record size from remaining capacity and remembers prior length for later position fixup, while also masking the type tag to its defined bits. Emission refuses invalid names and narrow inode truncation and user faults and disallowed signal contexts, using distinct negative outcomes for invalid and overflow and fault cases and stopping cleanly when space is exhausted.

Old single emitter allows at most one success per call, refuses invalid names and narrow inode truncation with distinct outcomes, and reports a fault if the user update fails. Its numeric outcome both signals completion and carries the error value.

Poll wait containers start with a defined wake routine plus current task linkage plus cleared trigger and error plus empty page chain and inline use count. Entry allocation prefers inline slots before paging, with page allocation failure recorded as out of memory. Teardown unlinks every registered wait and drops every file reference, then releases all extra pages.

Wait registration pins the file, records the wait address and interest key, and links a wake entry tied to the poll container. Wake delivery ignores events outside the recorded interest mask and otherwise marks the container triggered before performing a task wakeup through a transient entry.

Poll sleeping enters the requested state and only blocks when the triggered flag is clear, using an absolute timeout when supplied. After waking it returns to running state and clears the trigger under ordering guarantees that pair with the wake path and with queue insertion for the next check.

Descriptor set transfer treats a missing user pointer as an all clear request rather than a fault, with sizing derived from descriptor count rounded to machine words. Fetch brings user words in, store pushes result words out, and clearing writes zeros over the computed byte span.

Timeout completion restores the saved signal mask unless a non restarting interruption occurred, leaves sticky and zero timeouts untouched, and otherwise writes back the remaining interval in the caller selected representation. Writeback failure on read only caller memory preserves a successful return while converting a restartable interruption into a plain interruption.

Select progresses through validation of requested bits against open descriptors, followed by repeated scan and sleep cycles. Each scan queries interested descriptors with a key derived from requested classes, accumulates readiness counts and result bits, and disables further queueing once progress is seen. The cycle exits on readiness, expiry, signal, or recorded allocation failure, with an optional busy consideration that can shortcut sleeping.

Listing iteration starts with an emitter bound to a count and buffer, repeatedly offers entries to the emitter until it declines, then patches the trailing record position from the final iteration position when at least one record was placed.
The maximum select slack ceiling equals one hundred milliseconds expressed in nanosecond units.

Readiness groupings associate input interest with read norm plus read band plus poll in plus hangup plus error plus invalid indications, output interest with write band plus write norm plus poll out plus error plus invalid indications, and exception interest with priority plus invalid indications.
Descriptor set granularity equals bits in a machine word, with word count rounding up from descriptor count and byte count scaling by word size.

Timeout representation distinguishes native timeval from old 32 bit timeval from native timespec from old 32 bit timespec, each identified by a small integer tag starting at zero and increasing by one in the listed order.

User buffer interaction carries fault risk in every listing and select path with failed user writes during record emission or final position fixup or timeout writeback converting to fault failures, and malformed or truncated inputs converting to invalid or overflow failures without partial state exposure beyond documented accounting.

Wake marking runs under waitqueue synchronization yet still orders the trigger store with an explicit write barrier, while the sleeper clears the trigger with a full barrier that pairs for visibility and prevents clearing from passing the next event check. Initial queue insertion provides the ordering for the first iteration.
